subject: POC: Capacity & Success Criteria - Acme AI
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex@acme-ai.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC recap & next steps (capacity + success criteria)

Alex — great to meet today. Quick recap from our discovery + agreed next steps so we have a single source of truth for the POC kickoff. Happy to adjust if I missed anything.

Summary (what we covered)
- Objective: 2-week POC to validate latency/throughput goals for Acme's chat assistant and confirm cost profile for production serving.
- Workloads: mixed prompt sizes (~50–400 tokens), 70% short-turn chat, 30% longer generative flows. Expected steady-state test load ~35 req/s; peak bursts ~120 req/s for short windows.

Success criteria (what Acme wants validated)
- Latency: p95 generation latency <= 300ms at steady-state load (35 req/s).
- Throughput: system maintains >= 35 req/s with <1% error rate.
- Quality: model output matches baseline eval set (we'll run the 150-case prompt set you shared) with no regressions >5% in key metrics.
- Cost sanity check: projected cost per 1k tokens within target range you provided (internal).

Capacity / infra plan (prelim)
- Reserved GPUs: start with 2 reserved A10-class GPUs for baseline tests (expected to cover steady-state for multi-request batching).
- Autoscale policy: scale out to up to 6 GPUs on sustained increased load; scale triggers: CPU/GPU utilization > 70% for 90s or queue latency > 250ms.
- Burst behavior: we can support short bursts up to 120 req/s by over-provisioning ephemeral capacity (burst pool) — expected warm-up ~20–40s depending on cache hit rates.

Ownership & contacts
- Redwood sales & POC lead: Marissa Cole (me) — overall project owner, SOW/contract coordination.
- Redwood engineering lead: Sean Gallagher — performance testing and infra configs.
- Acme engineering lead: Alex Chen — test data access, eval set, and staging endpoints.
- Procurement: procurement@acme-ai.com — contract/SOW review.

Next steps (actions & timeline)
1) I'll send a short SOW and capacity estimate (attached) by EOD tomorrow (Oct 21). — Marissa
2) Alex provides the eval prompt set + staging endpoint credentials by Oct 23. — Alex
3) We schedule baseline load test for week of Oct 26 (target Oct 27). — Marissa & Sean to coordinate.
4) Procurement review & sign SOW (Acme) — target Oct 30.

Attachments: poc_capacity_estimate.pdf, poc_runbook.docx (drafts)

Thanks — excited to get this kicked off.

—
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: POC recap & next steps (capacity + success criteria)

Thanks Alex — answers inline below and attached the SOW + capacity estimate (poc_capacity_estimate.pdf) and a short runbook (poc_runbook.docx).

> Can you confirm the exact GPU class for reserved/scale units (A10 vs A100)?
- Recommendation: start the POC on 2x NVIDIA A10g (cost-effective for mixed token sizes and supports our batching optimizations). If you want to test A100 performance, we can run a short comparative test during the POC and share perf/cost delta.

> Does the SOW include a short penalty-free termination window?
- Yes. The draft SOW includes a 14-day evaluation window during which either party can terminate the reserved-capacity portion without penalty; we'll include explicit language for procurement to review.

Capacity notes / more detail on autoscale & burst handling:
- Warm cache vs cold-cache: first-run latency will be higher; we recommend a warm-up step (seed the KV cache with the eval prompt set) before any head-to-head measurement.
- Autoscaling mechanics: Redwood will pre-warm instances in the burst pool once queue latency crosses 120ms and predicted load spikes based on recent traffic. This typically brings warm-up down to ~20s for previously-seen contexts.
- Cost control: we recommend session-level prefix caching + 4s request coalescing to reduce token generation costs during spikes.

Proposed concrete timeline:
- Oct 23: Acme uploads eval set + creds.
- Oct 26–27: Redwood performs warm-up & baseline load test (Marissa/Sean running tests).
- Oct 28–29: Validation window; compare logs/metrics & iterate on batching/quantization profiles.
- Oct 30: Procurement decision & sign (target).

Next steps for us this week:
- Marissa: finalize SOW + include termination clause language (done, attached).
- Sean: prep load test harness and share test plan by EOD Oct 22.
- Dylan: confirm autoscale thresholds and burst pool size for the SOW (see note below).

Dylan — can you confirm recommended burst pool sizing for 120–140 req/s spikes (2–3 minute windows) given 2 reserved A10s and 6 max scale target?

—

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>

On Thu, Oct 22, 2026 at 11:30 AM Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com> wrote:
> Dylan — can you confirm recommended burst pool sizing for 120–140 req/s spikes (2–3 minute windows) given 2 reserved A10s and 6 max scale target?

Quick note on sizing:
- With our A10 perf profile and typical prompt distribution you provided, 2 reserved A10s should handle ~30–40 steady req/s with batching. For 120–140 req/s spikes we recommend the burst pool be sized for an additional 3 GPUs (so total concurrent GPUs = 5) to keep queue latency < 200ms during the spike window.
- Autoscale timing: pre-warm start when queue latency > 120ms observed for 30s; ramp adds 1 GPU every 20–30s (configurable). With pre-warm heuristics we expect effective warm-up ~20s for repeated contexts.
- If you want more conservative headroom for demo days, set max scale to 6 GPUs (we can include budget delta in SOW).

I'll add these numbers into the SOW and capacity_estimate doc and re-upload.

Dylan Brooks
Sr. Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
